Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test asserts that words with characters separated by 'H' or 'W' which map to the same Soundex code should ignore the second character. The current bug report highlights a problem in the Soundex.getMappingCode method specifically around the HW rule implementation. On examining the code snippet for getMappingCode(String str, int index), indeed the condition on line 192 causes a character to be skipped not only if it matches the code of the character two positions before (preHWChar), but also if the character two positions before is itself 'H' or 'W'. This introduces incorrect behavior because the algorithm should only suppress encoding when two characters that map to the same code are separated by 'H' or 'W'. The current implementation erroneously suppresses encoding if the character at index-2 itself is 'H' or 'W', which is not per the Soundex specification. This explains why the test fails for cases like "Ashcraft" and "Ashcroft" where the 'C' should be ignored (correct) but 'HW' characters should not cause broader suppression as currently implemented.

Hence, the bug arises due to the condition on line 192 using `firstCode == mappedChar || 'H' == preHWChar || 'W' == preHWChar` rather than strictly checking equality of mapped codes separated by an 'H' or 'W' as the Soundex HW rule specifies. Fixing this condition to correctly implement the rule will resolve the test failure and conform to the Soundex standard.

No recent bug reports appear relevant or contradictory, so the diagnosis relies mainly on the current bug report, failing test, and method code.

Suggested fix location: Soundex.getMappingCode(java.lang.String,int)
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test expects the Soundex encoding to follow the HW rule correctly: if two characters that map to the same code are separated by 'H' or 'W', the second character should not be encoded. The issue report points out a bug in the implementation of the HW rule in the `Soundex.getMappingCode` method.

Looking at the method `getMappingCode(String str, int index)`, when checking the HW rule (lines 187-195), the code uses the condition on line 192:

`if (firstCode == mappedChar || 'H' == preHWChar || 'W' == preHWChar)`

to determine whether to ignore encoding for the current character. It incorrectly prevents encoding if the character two positions before is 'H' or 'W', regardless of the mapping code. According to the Soundex specification, only if the character two positions before maps to the same code as the current character and the character in between is 'H' or 'W' should the second character be skipped.

Because of this, characters preceded by two 'H' or 'W' characters are not encoded correctly, causing test failures like the one on `testHWRuleEx1()`. For example, "Ashcraft" should be encoded as "A261", but the current rules incorrectly exclude or include characters violating the standard.

Thus, the bug arises from the HW rule condition in `Soundex.getMappingCode` being incorrectly implemented, leading to incorrect suppression of character encoding.

The best method to fix is `Soundex.getMappingCode(java.lang.String,int)`.

Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
